title: Three tab bar active-state treatments on magenta (underline / notch dot / tinted tile)

color.method: Pixel sampling via median-cut quantization of the supplied JPEG/GIF (compressed images, so values are approximate within a few units). Entries marked 'approx' were judged by eye, not sampled.
palette: magenta-pink background and accent (~51% of image)
color.roles: Two-color system: white UI on a saturated magenta field; the same magenta marks active items.

observed.layout: Three white rounded bars stacked on a magenta field, each with 5 items (Home, Search, Likes, Notifications, Profile). Bar 1: icons only, underline under Home. Bar 2: icons with labels; the bar has a small round notch with a dot above the active Notifications; active icon and label turn magenta. Bar 3: active Home sits in a rounded-square tinted tile with magenta icon and bold label.
observed.hierarchy: Active is the only magenta element in each bar.
observed.typography: Neo-grotesque small labels (Helvetica/Arial-like), semi-bold for active.

implementation_notes: Notch + dot: a cutout in the bar shape (SVG/mask) with a small dot in the cut; harder to build than underline or tile.
Tinted tile: accent at ~15-20% opacity behind icon + label.

concept_work.essence: Three levels of indicator effort (underline, notch, tile) shown on the same icon set.
what_makes_it_work: Color change on active icon and label creates a clear second cue.
Saturated background makes the white bar pop.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Magenta on white for small text may be near the contrast limit; needs checking.
Notch variant is the least robust: it must follow the active item and be animated.
Bar 1 has no labels and gives less accessibility support.

lessons: Pair a color change with a shape change so state is not color-only.
Rank indicator treatments by implementation cost as well as looks.
